newsitem.title: CHINA: China must increase share-holding firms - official.
newsitem.headline: China must increase share-holding firms - official.

text.p: China should support formation of share-holding companies as a way to help to ease capital shortages among state enterprises, an official of a research institute under the National Administration of State Property said on Tuesday.
"Share-holding companies offer a better way to raise capital," said Wei Jie, head of the research institute.
State enterprises that have not issued stock register sharper losses than share-holding companies, he said.
China should also convert shares held by the state directly and by state institutions as "legal person" shares to listed shares, Wei said.
"We should also consider allowing state shares and legal person shares to be changed into preferred stock," he said.
Legal person shares were created to inject funds into cash-strapped state companies while retaining state control by turning ownership over to cash-rich state institutions.
Brokers have speculated that Beijing would allow such shares to be listed to help to boost liquidity and curb speculation on the China's two stock markets.
